s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of painful vision loss with extensive lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Blurred vision and loss of vision in the left lower quadrant
Vitreous haze and optic-nerve pallor in the left eye
key_facts: 63-year-old white man
3-week history of redness of the left eye
Extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy
Blurred vision and loss of vision in the left lower quadrant
Supraorbital pain in both eyes
No fever, chills, weight loss, rash, or joint pains
Several weeks of malaise
Visual acuity 20/20 in the right eye and 20/125 in the left
Intraocular pressure 11 mm Hg in the right eye and 32 mm Hg in the left
Slit-lamp examination showed 1+ cell in the right eye, 4+ cell in the left
Gelatinous layered hypopyon with red-blood-cell layering in both eyes
Dilated exam revealed 1+ vitreous haze and optic-nerve pallor in the left eye
B-scan ultrasonography showed no retinal detachment or masses
Anterior chamber paracentesis of the left eye yielded only acellular, dense, proteinaceous material

shortlist.label: Intraocular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with panuveitis, extensive lymphadenopathy, and vision loss, consistent with lymphoma involvement of the eye

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause panuveitis, vision loss, and lymphadenopathy, and is a type of lymphoma that affects the central nervous system

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: A rare autoimmune disorder that can cause panuveitis, vision loss, and lymphadenopathy, and is a plausible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause panuveitis, vision loss, and lymphadenopathy, and is a systemic disease that can affect multiple organs

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: A broad category of cancer that can cause lymphadenopathy and vision loss, and is a plausible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of panuveitis, extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy, and a gelatinous layered hypopyon with red-blood-cell layering in both eyes, along with the absence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss, and the presence of acellular, dense, proteinaceous material in the anterior chamber paracentesis, are highly suggestive of intraocular lymphoma.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: While this condition can cause intraocular symptoms, the lack of central nervous system symptoms and the specific ocular findings make it less likely.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with granulomatous uveitis, skin, and hair findings, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause uveitis, but the presence of lymphadenopathy and the specific ocular findings are more suggestive of lymphoma.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma is a possible diagnosis, the term is too broad and intraocular lymphoma is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's symptoms and findings.
